evidence.claim: Novelis restarted hot mill operations at Oswego, New York after fires damaged the facility; the plant has capacity of about 1.7 billion pounds of aluminum sheets per year and is a major automotive and beverage supplier. Ford said it would continue to source finished materials from the plant and alternative sources.
evidence.source_title: Novelis restarts Oswego hot mill months after fires

evidence.claim: WRVO reported that automakers use rolled aluminum from Novelis Oswego to make vehicles lighter and described Ford as Novelis' biggest customer.
evidence.source_title: Novelis says its hot mill is back up and running after two devastating fires last fall

evidence.claim: Constellium’s Bowling Green, Kentucky plant produces flat rolled aluminum Auto Body Sheet products for the North American automotive market, with stated annual capacity of 100,000 metric tons.
evidence.source_title: Bowling Green, Kentucky, U.S. - Locations | Constellium

memory_update.text: CSTM should be promoted as the cleanest US-listed underfollowed direct exposure for automotive aluminum body sheet capacity; key diligence is whether it gained volume/share or pricing power during the Novelis Oswego outage.

KALU belongs in the underfollowed lane as an adjacent automotive aluminum extrusions/specialty-products processor, but its direct substitution for auto body sheet remains unproven and needs customer/program evidence.

CENX is only a speculative_shadow upstream aluminum candidate; keep it unless evidence shows auto-linked domestic metal premiums, rolling-mill customer ties, or policy support tied to automotive aluminum supply resilience.
Ford should be retained as a reference/customer-dependency anchor rather than a primary beneficiary; its disclosures may reveal which suppliers absorbed emergency demand.
Need a dedicated pass on private/non-US assets such as Novelis, Arconic, UACJ/Tri-Arrows, and other qualified mills because they may explain dependency even if not directly US-listed candidates.

node: Automotive aluminum sheet and specialty rolling capacity
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the automotive aluminum rolling bottleneck. The Novelis Oswego outage/restart is the dependency signal: one large domestic rolling asset appears important enough to disrupt automaker supply chains, especially Ford. The investable discovery lane should prioritize US-listed alternate auto body sheet capacity, adjacent automotive aluminum extrusions/components, and domestic primary aluminum suppliers that could benefit indirectly if OEMs diversify sourcing. This is not a trade recommendation; candidates are research leads with explicit evidence gaps.
